  go test ./...             PASSED

  staticcheck ./...         not installed - not checked
  errcheck ./...            not installed - not checked
  govulncheck ./...         not installed - not checked

Do not report these mechanically checked categories: build errors, vet diagnostics (printf verb mismatches, lost cancel, copied locks), formatting in the checked files only, failing tests, and a data race on a path the tests execute.

What these tools cannot see: the race detector only observes paths the tests actually executed, so untested concurrent code is unchecked. errcheck finds discarded errors, not errors caught and handled wrongly. govulncheck finds known vulnerabilities in dependencies, not unsafe handling of input in this code. No tool here judges whether a name misleads a reader, whether a function has grown too long to follow, or whether this change will be easy to extend without editing existing behaviour.

A clean tool run is not evidence a problem is absent; it is evidence that one specific tool did not see it.

These seven things no tool can check. Each one names what breaks.

1. An error returned without naming the operation reaches the caller
   as "no such file" with nothing saying what was being opened.
   Wrap it: fmt.Errorf("loading config %s: %w", path, err).

2. Every method on an interface must be implemented by every
   implementer and every test fake. A six-method interface makes
   adding a seventh a change to all of them. Keep interfaces to the
   methods the caller actually uses, declared where they are used.

3. Package-level state that can be written is reachable from every
   function in the package and from every test. It cannot be
   substituted, so code reading it cannot be tested without it, and
   tests touching it cannot run at once. Declare variables inside
   functions and pass dependencies in. If a value must live at
   package level, make it const. Go cannot make a slice or map
   const, so return a copy from a function instead.

4. A goroutine with no stated way to stop leaks. It appears as
   memory growth in production and never in a test, and the race
   detector cannot see it. Whoever starts it says in a comment how
   it ends.

5. Unexporting an identifier later breaks every caller; exporting
   one later breaks nobody. Export only what a caller outside the
   package must reach.

6. An abbreviated name (cfg, msg, n, v) makes every later reader
   rebuild its meaning from surrounding code. The author pays once,
   each reader pays again.

7. A doc comment that restates the signature goes stale without
   anyone noticing and then actively misleads. An exported symbol
   carrying no doc comment, or a non-obvious branch carrying no
   stated reason, forces every later reader to reconstruct the
   intent from the code -- and the maintainer who reconstructs it
   wrong deletes a guard believing it was incidental. Say why the
   thing exists and what breaks without it; leave obvious code
   uncommented.

Respond with a JSON array. Every element must be an object with exactly these keys:
  "file": string, the path from the diff
  "line": integer, the line number in the new file
  "severity": one of "critical", "high", "medium", "low"
  "message": string, one sentence describing the problem

Respond with the JSON array and nothing else. No prose, no explanation, no headings.
